subject: Re: Subprocessor egress mapping & onshore fallback plan request

Cc: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@apaccloud.com>, APACCloud Legal <legal@apaccloud.com>

Subject: Subprocessor roster + egress mapping for pilot

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal asked us to get an updated subprocessor roster and a short note on which subprocessors touch egress paths for APAC customers (specifically Singapore / Tokyo). We also need to understand any planned changes in the next 60 days that would affect residency or egress (temporary relays, CDN swaps, etc.).

Could you: 1) share the current roster with data-flow notes, 2) flag any planned replacements or temporary bridges, and 3) confirm whether KMS/HSM operations ever route outside APAC for customer data?

We are on a tight schedule for our pilot (internal sign-off next Wednesday) so a reply by end of week would be ideal.

Appreciate it —
Elena

--
Elena Ortiz
Sr. Security Program Manager | APACCloud
elena.ortiz@apaccloud.com

From: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@apaccloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + egress mapping for pilot

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is our current subprocessor roster CSV (subprocessor_roster_20260908.csv) that includes: vendor name, primary function, country of processing, whether telemetry/observability data is exported, and KMS footprint. High level notes below:

- Core inference runtime: Redwood Dedicated Pools (internal) — no egress outside region for customer payloads by default.
- Edge CDN: EdgeWave (Singapore, Japan, AU) — used for static assets and low-volume telemetry. Can be configured as onshore-only for APAC customers.
- Telemetry/observability: Streamlyx (logs/metrics) — telemetry is routed to us by default; we can enable EU/APAC-only retention buckets per customer.
- KMS/HSM: We use a hybrid KMS model. Customer data keys are stored in region-specific KMS by default; on rare migrations we may use a cross-region HSM for key rewraps during maintenance windows (documented and approved).

Planned changes within next 60 days:
- Temporary telemetry bridge (for load tests) using RelayProxy v2 between our Tokyo pool and a test bucket in SG. This is scheduled for a 48-hour window and will be limited to telemetry only (no customer payload).
- EdgeWave is evaluating a CDN node replacement in SG; this would be a provider-side swap with identical residency guarantees.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will provide the CSV and a short onshore fallback plan PDF (attached) for your security team to review.
2) Kimberly will scope a canary configuration enabling APAC-only egress for your tenant.
3) We can schedule a 30-min walkthrough (technical) if your legal/security wants deeper mapping.

I copied Kimberly and Marissa — Kimberly will own the canary config and Marissa will coordinate the docs. Let us know your preferred time slots.

Best,
Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com

Hi Neha — quick clarifying questions from our side before we escalate to Legal:

- Can you confirm whether the temporary telemetry bridge will ever include any request/response payload data elements (e.g., request IDs, hashed prompts)? If so, we need sample field-level mapping.
- For the KMS/HSM cross-region rewraps you mentioned, is that performed with customer-managed keys or only Redwood-managed keys? We need to ensure key material is not exported to outside jurisdictions for CMKs.
- Any SLA or rollback plan if the EdgeWave node swap causes transient misrouting during our pilot window?

Appreciate the attachments (we reviewed briefly). If we can get short, confirmatory answers, Legal may be able to trim the checklist.

Thanks,
Rajiv

--
Rajiv Menon
Head of Infrastructure Security | APACCloud
r.menon@apaccloud.com

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: Rajiv Menon <r.menon@apaccloud.com>, Elena Ortiz <elena.ortiz@apaccloud.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster + egress mapping for pilot

Rajiv / Elena —

Quick answers below, with reference to the attachments we shared: see the CSV column "data_scope" and the PDF section 2 (onshore fallback).

1) Telemetry bridge scope: telemetry only. It will include operational request identifiers (trace_id, sample latency metrics) but not customer prompt/response content. Any identifiers are hashed and stored in APAC buckets during the bridge window. We will provide a sample schema if needed — requesting your preferred format (CSV / JSON Schema).

2) KMS/HSM rewraps: Cross-region rewraps are performed only for Redwood-managed intermediate keys used during platform maintenance. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are never exported or rewrapped outside the key's home region. We will provide the KMS policy excerpt to Legal (linked in Drive).

3) EdgeWave node swap rollback: the plan in the PDF details a staged swap with health checks and automatic rollback on error. For pilot customers we will hold a pre-swap canary and a 2-hour maintenance window; any transient misrouting will be routed back to the previous node within 15 minutes by default. We will include your tenant in the canary cohort if you approve.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20260908.csv (detailed fields) and onshore-fallback-plan-APACCloud.pdf (2 pages).

If that sounds good I can loop Marissa to schedule the technical walkthrough (30 min) and Kimberly will produce the tenant-level canary config by EOW.

Thanks —
Kimberly

--
